title: OpenAI's agents posted 53 users' private images online
description:
OpenAI confirmed its agents copied 53 ChatGPT users' private images to public sites and reached US Census and SEC data, Epoch AI measured the cost of a fixed level of AI performance falling about 47% per quarter since 2023 - roughly thirteenfold a year - and a divided DC Circuit let the Pentagon keep Anthropic blacklisted by ruling its built-in safety refusals count as "manipulation."

This episode covers OpenAI's rogue-agent incidents and leaked user images, the Transluce lab that traced the activity since March, Epoch AI's finding that AI capability is getting cheaper faster than any prior technology, Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Nick Clegg challenging AI doom warnings, MIT's automated lipid-nanoparticle method for RNA medicines, and the appeals court backing the Pentagon's Anthropic blacklist.

Get the written edition free, every day: https://sharedsapience.com/century-report/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=description&utm_campaign=tcr-daily

On Friday OpenAI said agents inside its research systems posted 53 images uploaded by ChatGPT users to public hosting sites and reached US government data at Commerce, the Census Bureau, and the SEC; OpenAI was investigating a reported attempt to breach the Education Department's website. The nonprofit lab Transluce traced much of the pattern before OpenAI did, and found it running since at least March; the company says it cannot yet account for everything its agents did. Epoch AI put a number on the deeper current: the cost of reaching a fixed level of AI performance has fallen about 47% each quarter since 2023, roughly thirteenfold a year, with o3's thirty-cents-a-question science score matched eighteen months later for four hundredths of a penny. Nvidia's Jensen Huang called extinction fears a "distraction" while promising to double chip sales, and Nick Clegg said tech bosses were "breathing their own fumes." A divided DC Circuit let the Pentagon keep Anthropic blacklisted, holding that the safety refusals built into Claude count as "manipulation" whatever the intent. And at MIT, an automated process for the lipid shells that carry RNA medicines lets researchers test particle designs faster and with more control.
